Interface SlowQueryReportJmxMBean

All Known Subinterfaces:
SlowQueryReportJmx.RegistrationMBean
All Known Implementing Classes:
SlowQueryReportJmx, SlowQueryReportJmx.Registration
public interface SlowQueryReportJmxMBean
JMX MBean interface for exposing slow query statistics via JMX.

The resource published for a pool name is SlowQueryReportJmx.Registration, exposed as a Standard MBean, so this interface is the whole management surface: a public method of the resource that is not declared here stays invisible to a JMX client - only the notification methods contributed by NotificationEmitter come on top. Everything an operator needs, and everything the interceptor's mbeans-descriptors.xml advertises, therefore has to be declared here.

Each pool publishes its own MBean, under tomcat.jdbc:type=org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.SlowQueryReportJmx,name=<pool> unless the objectName interceptor property overrides it, and only when the interceptor is configured with notifyPool=false. With the default notifyPool=true no MBean is registered and the statistics are only observable through the connection pool's own MBean. A second live pool trying to publish under a name that is already occupied is refused by the MBean server; sharing one name between live pools is not supported.

notifyPool itself is deliberately not part of this interface. It is a per-interceptor-instance configuration property - the pool builds one interceptor chain per pooled connection and configures every instance with it - and every instance decides the routing of its own notifications from its own copy when it reports a query. Writing it through JMX would change only the single instance that happens to own the registration and leave the pool's other connections routing as before, so the attribute would promise a pool-wide effect it could not deliver. It stays a configuration entry point, applied to every instance of the pool by SlowQueryReportJmx.setProperties(java.util.Map).

  • Method Details

    • getPoolName

      String getPoolName()
      Returns the registration name of the connection pool this MBean reports for, as the PoolName attribute. The registration, the notifications and the statistics belong to that one pool; a second live pool configured with the same name does not share this MBean, and its registration is refused while this one holds the name.

      The value is recorded when the pool starts. It is not cleared when the pool's chain is released, so it can remain non-null after the MBean has been given up; only an instance that was never bound to a pool answers null.

      Returns:
      the pool's recorded registration name, or null before this instance is bound to a pool

    • getPoolNames

      String[] getPoolNames()
      Returns the names of all the connection pools this JVM currently holds recorded query statistics for, as the PoolNames attribute. That is a JVM-wide view, not this pool alone: a pool using the plain SlowQueryReport interceptor, which never registers an MBean of its own, appears here as well, and pools configured with the same name appear once.
      Returns:
      the names of the pools that currently hold a statistics map; an empty array when no pool has registered statistics

    • resetStats

      void resetStats()
      Removes all query statistics recorded for the pool this MBean reports for, so an operator can start from a clean slate instead of restarting the pool. Only that pool's store is cleared; another live pool's statistics are untouched, even if it shares the name (a configuration the pool does not support for JMX publication). Only the recorded content is dropped: the pool stays monitored and keeps accumulating statistics afterwards, and a query recorded again starts from empty counters.

    • getSlowQueriesCD

      CompositeData[] getSlowQueriesCD() throws OpenDataException
      Returns slow query statistics as JMX CompositeData, as the SlowQueriesCD attribute. The element schema is SlowQueryReport.QueryStats: every duration (maxInvocationTime, minInvocationTime, totalInvocationTime, prepareTime) is in milliseconds and every date field (maxInvocationDate, minInvocationDate, lastInvocation) is epoch milliseconds.
      Returns:
      array of composite data representing slow query statistics
      Throws:
      OpenDataException - if the composite data cannot be created; a JMX client gets it wrapped in an MBeanException
